launch-desk.title: Aurelith launches the Visor mixed-reality headset
launch-desk.author: Inez Calder
body: [f01: Aurelith launched the Visor on Monday, its first mixed-reality headset.] [f02: The Visor costs $1,499.] [f03: It ships December 4.]
[f04: At launch, it will only be sold in the US and Canada.] [f05: The headset weighs 545 g.]

That's a premium price for a first-generation product from a company that has never sold a headset. Aurelith is pitching comfort over raw specs, a bet aimed at people who tried a headset once and put it back in the box. The next few weeks of reviews will show whether that bet pays off.

byteward.title: Aurelith launches its Visor mixed-reality headset
byteward.author: Arlo Pennick
body: [f01: Aurelith on Monday introduced the Visor, the company's first mixed-reality headset.] [f02: It's priced at $1,499.]
[f06: Each eye gets its own 3,400 by 3,400 pixel display.] [f07: Aurelith rates the battery for 2.5 hours of use.]
[f08: The Visor's app store will open with 320 apps.] That's a modest library, and Aurelith will need developers to keep building for it.

frametime.title: Aurelith's Visor mixed-reality headset is here
frametime.author: Kofi Mensah-Lind
body: [f01: Aurelith's first mixed-reality headset, the Visor, launched today.] We put it through our usual game tests.

[f09: In our testing, 10 of the 12 games we tried held a steady 90 frames per second.] [f10: The toughest, Glasshollow, averaged 71 fps at high settings.] Dips like that are easy to feel in a headset, so we'd drop that game to medium.
[f07: Aurelith quotes 2.5 hours of battery life.] [f11: In our gaming runs, the battery lasted 2 hours and 10 minutes.] That's enough for a long session, though not a marathon.

ohm-and-bit.title: Aurelith unveils the Visor mixed-reality headset
ohm-and-bit.author: Imogen Vale
body: [f01: Aurelith has unveiled the Visor, its first mixed-reality headset.] The interesting part is how Aurelith kept the weight down.
[f05: The headset itself weighs 545 g.] [f12: The battery rides in a separate 210 g pack on a cable.] Moving it off the head takes weight off your face, at the cost of a cord running down your back.
[f06: Behind the lenses sit two 3,400 by 3,400 pixel displays, one per eye.] [f13: The field of view is 100° horizontally.] That's on the narrow side, a common price of compact optics.
[f14: Apps never see raw eye-tracking data, only the moment the wearer confirms a selection.] It's a sensible design, and it limits what a rogue app could learn.

bench-and-bill.title: Aurelith launches the Visor headset
bench-and-bill.author: Celia Marchetti
body: [f01: Aurelith released the Visor, its first mixed-reality headset, on Monday.] Its eye tracking is where the legal questions start.

[f15: Aurelith says raw eye-tracking data is processed on the headset and never sent to its servers.] [f14: Apps get only the wearer's selections, not the gaze data itself, under the company's developer terms.]
[f16: A pending bill, the Gaze Data Privacy Act, would ban the sale of eye-tracking data.] [f17: Companies that break it would face fines of up to $7,500 per affected user.]
For now, Aurelith's promises are voluntary, and a privacy policy can change with a single update.

wirefold.title: Aurelith launches Visor mixed-reality headset
body: Aurelith on Monday launched the Visor, its first mixed-reality headset, priced at $1,499 and shipping December 4 in the US and Canada.
